dedupe_keys.name: agent based model of firm level adaptation and intermediation in networked fresh food markets the bogota potato market comses

description: This agent-based model simulates competition in the potato market of Bogotá, Colombia, and explores the economic impact of intermediaries on the potato supply chain. It accompanies the paper by Mejía and García-Díaz, Market-level effects of firm-level adaptation and intermediation in networked markets of fresh foods: a case study in Colombia, Agricultural Systems 160 (2018). Firms in a networked market adapt their behaviour and may trade through intermediaries, so the model shows how intermediation and adaptation shape market outcomes. Coverage is the Bogotá potato supply chain. The NetLogo code, version 1.1.0 from April 2020, is free to download from the CoMSES Computational Model Library under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 licence. Caveats: it is a stylised research model of one commodity and city, parameters come from the authors' case study, and the non-commercial licence limits reuse. Simulation uses: testing how the loss of intermediaries or market links disrupts fresh food supply to a city, and exploring market network resilience in food supply chain studies. Related records: the Food Shocks Cascade model (model-food-shocks-cascade-fsc) works at international scale and the Kenya market locations (data-kenya-major-markets-finaccess) give market nodes for another country.
